title: Joe Espada’s status unchanged after Astros part ways with GM Dana Brown: Sources
content:
NEW YORK — Houston Astros manager Joe Espada’s status is unchanged in the wake of general manager Dana Brown’s dismissal Monday, according to two team sources who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal matters.

USA Today reported earlier Monday that a “high-ranking team official” told Espada he would not receive another contract after the season. USA Today’s report added that Espada was “given the choice of staying with the team through the duration of the season or departing now.” But Espada has had no conversations about his future, according to the two team sources.

Espada, who missed Sunday’s game while tending to a family emergency, is in New York with the club and will manage Tuesday’s series opener against the Yankees.

Like Brown was, Espada is working this season on the final year of his contract. Houston has not won a playoff game since Brown hired Espada to succeed Dusty Baker after the 2023 season. Espada, 50, has led the Astros to a 240-214 record across his 2 1/2 seasons in charge, including the 2024 AL West title.

His 2026 club entered Monday tied with the Texas Rangers atop the division at 65-66, but in first place via the tiebreaker Houston has already clinched over the Rangers.
